translation: It is also called the thigh bone (髀骨); its upper end is like a pestle and enters the mortar of the bishu (髀樞), and its lower end is like a hammer and connects to the hang bone (䯒骨); the whole is called the thigh (股), and is the general name for the two great branches of the lower body, commonly called the thigh bone (大腿骨). If one falls from a horse and is twisted and injured, with the bone broken and the sinew swollen, black-purple and cool, and white blisters rising on the outside, this is because the broken bone has leaked qi, and this condition is rarely cured by treatment. If the person is young with sufficient qi and blood, although the form and signs show swelling and pain without fainting, and there are no white blisters, it can be treated.
